key_insight: LLM-assisted qualitative analysis can work, but its quality depends heavily on the specific research context and workflow rather than model language ability alone.
clinical_relevance: For health research teams using LLMs to analyze interviews or other qualitative data, careful workflow design and human oversight are essential to preserve interpretive validity.
method: Translated framework analysis into bounded, sequential LLM-supported tasks
Applied the workflow to 20 Chinese-language interviews on fear of dementia (~150,000 characters)
Compared four multilingual LLM outputs plus a prior researcher-only analysis
evidence_signal: Sixteen experts produced 496 blinded item-level evaluations across analytical domains and qualitative quality dimensions, showing that all LLMs completed the workflow but rankings varied substantially.
watch_item: Results may not generalize beyond this specific qualitative topic, language, and workflow, so outputs should not be treated as interchangeable or automatically reliable.
paper_title: Context Matters in LLM-Assisted Qualitative Data Analysis: Workflow Development and Multidimensional Evaluation in Health Research
